newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone rebel commanders take envoys hostage.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel commanders take envoys hostage.

text.p: Rebel commanders in Sierra Leone seized its ambassador to Guinea and rebel officials who went for elections to replace Foday Sankoh as their leader, a member of the movement's political wing said on Monday.

Agnes Jalloh told Reuters that Revolutionary United Front (RUF) field commanders, apparently Sankoh loyalists, tricked the ambassador and officials from the RUF external delegation into crossing into Sierra Leone from Guinea on Saturday.

"The RUF delegation had been warned not to cross over to Sierra Leone (from Guinea) but the RUF field commanders deceived them... assuring them of their security and of their desire to replace Sankoh," she said in the capital Freetown.
Jalloh, whose husband is among three officials held, said they were seized in Kailahun district on Saturday evening.
The commanders had made no immediate demands, she added.

The RUF's external negotiators announced on March 15 that Sankoh was to be replaced as head of the movement because he had been blocking the peace process. At the time, they said that the move had the full backing of RUF field commanders.

Sankoh has been in Nigeria since early March. Officially, the Nigerians say he is a guest of the government but Nigeria's ambassador to Freetown has said he is under house arrest after trying to enter the country with a gun.
Nigeria is the regional power broker in West Africa.
Sankoh, who took up arms in 1991, signed a peace deal with civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah in Ivory Coast on November 30. Implementation has dragged.
